title: Distinct Polities, Connected Communities
definition: A community or group organized under a form of political authority.
content:
A polity is an organized political community. A sultanate is a polity headed by a sultan. Sulu and Maguindanao were distinct historical polities, not two names for one identical government. Communities in Mindanao and the Sulu islands also had different languages, livelihoods and local relationships. Religion alone does not describe every persons role or experience.

Our labelled relationship guide keeps Sulu and Maguindanao separate while showing that connections could exist between them. It is not a territorial map or a modern boundary claim. Ask which ruler, community, place and period a source concerns before combining accounts. Do not treat all of Mindanao as one sultanate or assume every person belonged to one religion. This chapter studies institutions and people respectfully; students do not need to disclose ancestry or faith to complete the investigation.

clues: Political community
A polity concerns organized authority; a sultanate is headed by a sultan.
Distinct examples
Sulu and Maguindanao were separate polities with connections.
Variation
One religion or regional label does not describe every community or person.
task: A caption treats Sulu and Maguindanao as two names for one identical government. What correction fits?
Keep the distinct polities visible and investigate their particular connections
Treat every community in Mindanao as identical
Use religion to assign every persons role
Call the teaching diagram a modern boundary map
reason: Keep the distinct polities visible and investigate their particular connections. One religion or regional label does not describe every community or person.

title: A Named Leader: Sultan Kudarat
definition: A relationship in which parties agree to work together for particular purposes.
content:
The NHCP marker identifies Sultan Dipatuan Kudarat as a sultan of Maguindanao who ruled from 1619 to 1671. It describes links with Sulu, opposition to Spanish forces and a peace agreement in 1645. This named example shows that leadership could involve alliances, conflict and negotiation at different times.

Keep the ruler, polity and period attached to the claim. A marker is a later public account, not the transcript of every meeting. We do not invent a speech or assume that a ruler spoke for every persons private wishes. The marker also does not turn the sultanate into the same thing as a present-day province named Sultan Kudarat. Our timeline identifies the dated leadership and agreement without drawing exact territorial borders or reenacting fighting. A fuller look at varied responses follows in Mission 4.

clues: Named leadership
The NHCP marker dates Kudarats rule to 1619-1671.

title: Trade Connected People and Work
definition: People and places connected through exchange of goods.
content:
Sulu was part of exchange networks, including connections with China, Maguindanao and Brunei. A maritime-history study describes these connections and the work behind goods moving through them. A sea route should not make us imagine empty islands or people whose lives consisted only of conflict. Producers, crews, traders and households had different activities and positions.

The same history also includes raids, captivity and coerced labor. Coerced means forced rather than freely chosen. These caused harm and should not be hidden behind a story of valuable cargo. Nor should the actions of particular people be assigned to every Muslim or every member of a community. Our source guide names exchange, work and unequal conditions without graphic scenes or a game of taking captives. We award careful historical explanation, never harm. One trading account does not establish every workers consent, payment or household outcome.

Open the three clues and choose an explanation they support. Use Explain for help or revisit the lesson before targeted practice if the topic needs review.
clues: Connections
Sulu had trading relationships with neighboring polities and wider markets.
Work and conditions
Exchange depended on work, which could include unequal and forced conditions.
No stereotype
Specific harmful actions do not define every person of a religion or community.
task: A cargo total is used to say all workers freely benefited. What should be checked?
Work, consent, payment and unequal conditions for the people involved
Nothing because valuable trade proves fairness
Whether every Muslim had one occupation
Whether all communities shared one private motive
reason: Work, consent, payment and unequal conditions for the people involved. Specific harmful actions do not define every person of a religion or community.

title: An Agreement Needed Follow-up Evidence
definition: Managing relationships through communication and negotiation.
content:
Polities could use diplomacy as well as face conflict. An agreement records terms or commitments. It does not automatically show how every term worked in practice or that every community had the same understanding. Ask who made it, when, which version you are reading and what evidence describes implementation.

Saleebys History of Sulu presents both Spanish and Sulu-text translations for the 1878 agreement. Their presence reminds us to inspect versions and perspectives rather than treat one wording as everyones complete experience. This mission does not settle every clause or a present-day territorial dispute. Our fictional source desk separates an agreement text, a later action record and a report of local conditions. Match each to what it can establish. A request for peace does not erase earlier harm, and signing does not guarantee equal power or permanent peace.

clues: Terms
An agreement records commitments or claims.
Versions
Check which text, translation and perspective a source presents.
Practice
Implementation and local effects need evidence beyond signing.
task: An agreement text is used to claim all terms worked identically everywhere. What should be checked?
Versions, implementation and local effects in the particular period
Nothing because signing guarantees every outcome

reason: Versions, implementation and local effects in the particular period. Implementation and local effects need evidence beyond signing.

title: Communities Were More Than Labels
definition: The standpoint and purpose from which a source presents information.
content:
Communities include people with varied roles and histories. The Sulu research discusses distinct groups, including Sama and Tausug, rather than one identical island population. Even a named group does not mean every member had one occupation, status or response. A ruler account is not automatically every households voice.

Historical sources also have perspectives. Saleebys 1908 book was produced in an American colonial setting and contains dated judgments; a later marker commemorates a leader; a research article asks its own questions. Compare them carefully and keep the source date visible. Our fictional portfolio has a ruler summary, an exchange entry and a community account. Each can help with some questions and leave gaps. We do not ask students to adopt a faith or repeat insulting colonial labels. Explain particular actions with evidence while respecting peoples dignity.

Open the three clues and choose an explanation they support. Use Explain for help or revisit the lesson before targeted practice if the topic needs review.
clues: Diversity
Sama, Tausug and other communities cannot be reduced to one identical experience.
Perspective
A source has a maker, purpose and date.
Scope
A ruler, institution or category does not automatically speak for every person.
task: A ruler summary is used as every households complete story. What correction fits?
Keep its scope and seek evidence about other roles and experiences
Assume every person shared identical conditions
Replace all local names with one stereotype
Treat a source as having no date or purpose
reason: Keep its scope and seek evidence about other roles and experiences. A ruler, institution or category does not automatically speak for every person.

title: Prepare Your Polities and Communities Report
definition: The standpoint and purpose from which a source presents information.
content: Review five ideas. Sulu and Maguindanao were distinct polities with connections. Kudarats dated leadership included alliance, opposition and negotiation. Trade involved people and work, including conditions that could be unequal or forced. Treaty texts need follow-up evidence of practice. Communities and sources contain different roles and perspectives. Prepare a fictional report for another Grade 5 learner. Name the polity, community, place and period. Connect a claim to a supporting clue and explain a limit. Do not merge every community into one government, erase harm behind valuable cargo, or turn particular harmful actions into a stereotype about a religion. Keep agreement texts separate from actual outcomes and historical questions separate from present-day legal claims. The main quiz has five questions and three correct passes. Return to linked learning content before practice and a retry if needed. Completing this mission earns its configured reward once, but does not complete Chapter 11. Complete all missions, then pass the chapter challenge to earn the chapter badge.

Sama, Tausug and other communities cannot be reduced to one identical experience.
Perspective
A source has a maker, purpose and date.

A ruler, institution or category does not automatically speak for every person.
task: Which report best uses this mission?
Keep distinct polities, people, actions and dated evidence visible without stereotypes
Treat every Muslim as having one role
Call every agreement proof of equal power and lasting peace
Use one ruler as every households complete history
reason: Explain distinct polities and communities through leadership, trade, diplomacy and source evidence while respecting dignity and limits.
